skill.name: image-edit
skill.description: Route image-edit requests to the best RunComfy model for the job. The skill covers batch identity-preserving edits, text replacement, multi-reference composition, local edits, and mask-based inpainting.
skill.summary: Route image edits to RunComfy models for precise, model-specific results.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown-formatting false positives, including fenced code markers, inline field names, placeholder HTTPS URLs, and ellipsis placeholders. The real concerns are intentional RunComfy CLI execution and external transfer of prompts, image URLs, masks, and generated outputs to RunComfy services. No prompt injection attempt or covert exfiltration instruction was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Pin the RunComfy CLI version, keep structured JSON inputs, and request confirmation before running edit commands.
Tell users that prompts, image URLs, masks, and outputs are processed by RunComfy before handling sensitive assets.
Prefer scoped tokens, rotate credentials regularly, and verify owner-only permissions for local token storage.

content.user_title: Edit Images with RunComfy Model Routing
content.value_statement: Choosing the wrong image model wastes time and produces weak edits. This skill routes each request to a suitable RunComfy image-edit model and gives focused prompting guidance.
actual_capabilities: Routes general and batch edits to Nano Banana Edit.
Routes multilingual text replacement and multi-reference composition to GPT Image 2 Edit.
Routes single-reference local edits to Flux Kontext Pro.
Routes mask-based object removal and region replacement to Z-Image Turbo Inpaint.
Documents required input fields, size limits, masks, seeds, and output options.
Provides RunComfy CLI invocation patterns for each supported route.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, and authentication.
Sends prompts, image URLs, masks, and generated outputs through RunComfy services.
Requires publicly fetchable HTTPS URLs for source images and masks.
Selects one route per call and inherits each model limit.

use_cases.title: Batch Product Image Updates
use_cases.description: Apply consistent background, resolution, and aspect changes across a product image set.

use_cases.title: Localized Marketing Assets
use_cases.description: Replace in-image headlines with multilingual text while preserving layout and brand marks.

use_cases.title: Precise Retouching and Cleanup
use_cases.description: Remove objects, replace masked regions, or make one focused local change to a source image.

prompt_templates.title: Simple Background Swap
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner edit with one source image
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit this image with RunComfy. Keep the subject unchanged and replace the background with a clean studio setting.

prompt_templates.title: Consistent Product Batch
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit these product images as a consistent square gallery. Preserve product shape, color, labels, and camera angle.

prompt_templates.title: Multilingual Poster Rewrite
prompt_templates.prompt: Replace only the poster headline with the supplied translated text. Keep the photo, logo, layout, and font weight unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Masked Region Replacement
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the mask to replace only the selected region. Preserve all unmasked areas, match lighting, and keep edges natural.

output_examples.input: A user asks to change three product backgrounds while keeping the products identical.
output_examples.output: The skill selects Nano Banana Edit, locks the square format, and prepares a batch-focused edit instruction.

output_examples.input: A user asks to replace an English poster headline with Japanese text.
output_examples.output: The skill selects GPT Image 2 Edit and instructs it to replace only the headline while preserving the layout.

output_examples.input: A user provides a mask for cables in a street photo and asks for cleanup.
output_examples.output: The skill selects Z-Image Turbo Inpaint and uses a low-strength removal prompt for the masked region.

best_practices: Put preservation requirements before the requested change.
Use small, specific edits instead of one broad compound request.
Confirm that image and mask URLs are safe to send to RunComfy.
anti_patterns: Do not send sensitive or private images without user approval.
Do not combine unrelated edits that require different model routes.
Do not omit masks when requesting precise inpainting.

faq.question: Does this skill edit images locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the local RunComfy CLI to submit image-edit jobs to RunComfy services.

faq.question: Which model does it choose by default?
faq.answer: It defaults to Nano Banana Edit when the user does not name a specific route.

faq.question: Can it edit several images at once?
faq.answer: Yes. Nano Banana Edit supports batch edits for one to twenty input images.

faq.question: Can it replace text inside an image?
faq.answer: Yes. It routes multilingual text replacement and layout-sensitive text edits to GPT Image 2 Edit.

faq.question: When should I use a mask?
faq.answer: Use a mask when the edit must affect only a specific region of the image.

faq.question: What data leaves my machine?
faq.answer: Prompts, image URLs, masks, and outputs may be processed by RunComfy services.
